resources.string: A profile says how an alarm treats you. The active one is for every mission left on Automatic, unless a rule below fits it. It decides from the next ring: an alarm already ringing keeps its handshake and its voice.
No profile is active. Choose one, or missions left on Automatic use the standard settings.
Each dial works alone. A setting is saved the moment you choose it.
Lines end as a suggestion: when you are ready.
Lines end as an invitation to begin.
Lines end by telling you to begin.
Lines end by telling you to begin now.
Lines end with an order to do it now.
No extra words. Never an insult, at any setting.

plurals.name: dial_obnoxiousness_density
plurals.item: Up to %1$d shout in a line. Never an insult.
Up to %1$d shouts in a line. Never an insult.

plurals.name: dial_obnoxiousness_repeats
plurals.item: The last one is said %1$d more time.
The last one is said %1$d more times.

resources.string: Rings %1$d times, for %2$s each, with %3$s between.
The voice is at its loudest.
Asks how it is going once, %1$s later.
Asks how it is going up to %1$d times, %2$s apart.
A fixed mission can be delayed or skipped with one tap. A flexible one always can.
A fixed mission asks you to confirm before a delay or a skip. A flexible one never asks.
A fixed mission asks for a reason before a delay or a skip. A flexible one never asks.
A fixed mission offers a way to start first, before a delay or a skip. A flexible one never asks.

plurals.name: dial_recovery_offers
plurals.item: When a start does not happen, offers once: %2$s.
When a start does not happen, offers up to %1$d times: %2$s.

resources.string: a smaller step, if the mission has one
How a ring opens, for a mission called %1$s
This director keeps a line to twelve words, so the extra words go first and firmness and obnoxiousness may not show.
This profile has a handshake of its own, so this dial changes nothing until it goes back to the standard handshake.

A rule gives a mission a profile by its category or the words in its title. A profile you pick for a mission itself comes first. If several rules fit, the one that says most decides: both a category and words, then words, then a category.
Asks for nothing, so it fits no mission
Its profile is gone, so this rule does nothing.
Missions it fits go back to their next choice from the next ring.
Leave it empty for any category.
Leave it empty for any title. Capital letters make no difference.
Fill in a category, words, or both. A rule that asks for nothing fits no mission.
Another rule asks for the same. Change that one instead.
